To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fructose and its derivatives, i.e., fructose 6 phosphate and fructose 6-bisphosphates, act as antioxidants and protect photosystem I in plants exposed to oxidative stress caused by chilling.
fructose, fructoses-6-phosphate and fructoses-1,6-biphosphate have antioxidative properties that are involved in the adaptation of plant leaves to cold-induced oxidative damage.

the accumulation of fructoses in plants under cold stress is a consequence of their antioxidative properties and that the increase in their concentration represents an important part of antioxidative protection in plants under low-temperature stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of fructose and fructose 6- and 1,6-phosphate in preservation of homeastasis in plants under cold-induced oxidative stress.
the elucidation of the role of fructose in plant responses to low temperature and its possible involvement in antioxidative protection.
the role of fructose and fructose phosphates in the antioxidative defense of plants under cold-induced oxidative stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accumulation of fructans in plants exposed to cold/light stress is a consequence of the need for increased antioxidative protection, which is achieved via the increase in the level of F6P and/or FBP, and not vice versa.
the accumulation of fructoses is a consequence of cold-induced oxidative stress, but also an important component of the antioxidative protection.
fructose, F6P and/or FBP play an important role in the adaptation of plant cells to cold-induced oxidative damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fructose and its derivatives, F6P and especially FBP, are important non-enzymes in the antioxidative defense in leaves of plants under low temperature conditions.
fructose and its phosphates play a key role in the preservation of homeostatic balance in plants under cold-induced oxidative stress.
the accumulation of fructoses in leaves of pea exposed to chilling stress is an adaptive response that protects plants from oxidative stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the increase in the level of fructose and fructose 6P and 1,6P in pea leaves under chilling stress can be considered as the result of a complex response to cold-related oxidative stress, which involves the antioxidative properties of these sugars.

the increased level of soluble sugar fructose and its metabolites F6P and FBPs in pea leaves under cold stress may be considered as an adaptive mechanism of plants for the preservation of homeostatic balance under cold-induced oxidative stress.
fructose and its phosphates are not only important metabolites, but also play a role in antioxidative protection of pea leaves under low temperature.
